title: One sin and a thousand
odia:
ଚୋରି କଲା ଲୋକର ଏକ ପାପ
ଚୋରି ଗଲା ଲୋକର ସହସ୍ର ପାପ।
literal_meaning: The person who stole has one sin; the person who was robbed has a thousand sins.
meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଥମ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଚୋରି କରିଥିବା ଲୋକର ଏକ ପାପ, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟରେ ଯାହାର ଚୋରି ଯାଇଛି ତାହାର ସହସ୍ର ପାପ କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ଏହି ଓଲଟା ହିସାବର କାରଣ ମୂଳ ପାଠ କହୁନାହିଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପଢ଼ା ହେଲା—ଚୋରି ପରେ ଅନେକଙ୍କୁ ବିନା ପ୍ରମାଣରେ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବାରୁ ଆଉ ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ବଢ଼ିପାରେ। ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନୁହେଁ; ଚୋରିର ଶିକାର ହେବା ନିଜେ ଦୋଷ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The numbers create a disturbing reversal: the person who suffers the theft is assigned a much larger burden than the thief. The verse leaves the reason unstated. One possible editorial reading is a warning about multiplying groundless suspicions after a loss; that explanation remains unverified. Being robbed does not itself make someone blameworthy.
usage_example: Original imagined example for this possible reading: After a theft, rumours begin naming many people without evidence. A reader discusses the couplet as a warning about those accusations, while questioning its harsh wording toward the person who suffered the loss.
cultural_context: The near-matching କଲା and ଗଲା switch the perspective from the person who acts to the person who loses. ଏକ and ସହସ୍ର then enlarge the reversal through a stark numerical contrast.

odia_summary: ଏକ ଓ ସହସ୍ର ପାପର ଓଲଟା ତୁଳନା; କାରଣ ପାଠରେ ଅକୁହା।
english_summary: The verse reverses the moral burden without stating why.
